references.text: Jacob commanded them and said: I will be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers in the cave that is on Ephron the Hittite's field.
Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, old and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
The life of Ishmael was one hundred and thirty-seven years. Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people.
Isaac breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. His sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
Die on the mountain you are climbing, and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron, your brother, died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed both of Joseph's sons, and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
A strong contrast between miraculous resurrection to life and the natural moment of death that leads to being gathered with the fathers.
Direct narrative connection linking Jacob's prophetic charge (49:1) with his death (49:33).
Theological parallel between the Old and New Testaments confirming that the death of believers is a 'gathering to the fathers'.
